_note: Industry, street, ownership, moat, gaps and conflicts as of 30-Sep-2026. Items compiled from sources dated on or before 30-Sep-2026; later items are in updates/later-facts.json.

market.fact: Global carbon black demand ~14.9 mn t in 2025, ~16.5 mn t by 2029; speciality carbon black ~1.06 mn t growing ~4% a year to ~1.25 mn t (Notch Consulting, cited in the FY26 annual report).

Management sizing (Q1FY27 call): speciality carbon black >1 mn t; super speciality ~300,000 t; carbon nanotubes ~30,000 t; global battery demand ~1.6 TWh in 2025 rising to ~6.8 TWh by 2035; ~50% LFP today, needing ~1.6 mn t of LFP and ~1.6 mn t of anode; China holds essentially all LFP capacity, the top 5-6 makers 75-80%.

Coal tar pitch is the binder for carbon anodes in aluminium smelting and for graphite electrodes; Himadri has 65%+ of India's pitch market and ~67% of naphthalene. Graphite-electrode makers face structural overcapacity and weak margins (FY26 annual report); HEG and Graphite India earned ROE of 7% and 3% in FY26.
Cell component prices (cathode and anode) fell 50-60% over the last 4-5 years (management, Q4FY26 call).

forces: Coal tar is a by-product of steel-making coke ovens; prices follow coal and crude. After the West Asia crisis (Apr-May 2026) input costs rose and Himadri passed them on: Q1FY27 realisation +23%, volume -6%.

Demand from plastics, inks, batteries and cables grows faster than tyre black; Himadri now has 130 kt of speciality capacity (the world's largest single site, per the company) and is adding super speciality grades.
Indian aluminium smelter expansions support pitch demand; graphite electrodes are oversupplied. Liquid pitch exports from Haldia and Mangalore open the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
PCBL is India's largest carbon black maker (FY26 revenue Rs 8,189 cr, EBITDA margin 12.7%, ROE 5%); global majors (Cabot, Orion, Birla Carbon) dominate speciality grades.
India's cell makers need local cathode and anode suppliers; but China supplies all LFP today at very low prices, and approvals take 1.5-2 years.
Indian tyre market ~USD 12 bn (FY25) growing 8-9% a year (annual report); Birla Tyres is a small re-entrant in agri, OTR and truck bias tyres against large incumbents.

moat: Scale and integration in coal tar
600 kt distillation, 65%+ of India's pitch, 8 plants, captive power, 292 heated tankers; by-products feed carbon black and speciality oils.
Lowest-cost Indian supplier; hard for a newcomer to collect enough coal tar.
Long relationships with steel makers' coke ovens and imports; no dependence on West Asia (management).
Feedstock security, but prices pass through both ways.
70+ grades, 130 kt capacity, EcoVadis Platinum; global majors still lead in high-end grades.
Mix shift is real; pricing power is not yet proven over a downturn.
Approved by major smelters (Hindalco, Vedanta, Nalco, Alba, EGA per the deck) and electrode makers.
Anode 200 tpa from Apr-2026; LFP 2,000 tpa from Q3FY27; no commercial orders disclosed.
Sub-scale revived brand against large incumbents.
gaps: Revenue, volume, price and margin by product (pitch, carbon black, speciality black, naphthalene, oils, SNF) are not disclosed; we model one core line using total standalone volume and consolidated core EBITDA.
EBITDA per tonne mixes consolidated core EBITDA with standalone volume; the small consolidated subsidiaries (China plant, Durofresh) add revenue without volume disclosure.
ICICI Securities' July-2026 SoTP components and multiples are not in public summaries; its EPS estimates are not public.
LFP pricing, raw-material sourcing and expected margins are not disclosed (management declined on the Q1FY27 call).
Birla Tyres' standalone profit and loss, and the split of the Others segment between tyres and mining by quarter, are not disclosed (FY26 tyre revenue Rs 187 cr is from the Q4 call).
Carrying values of the Sicona and IBC preference instruments could not be read cleanly from the annual report tables; only IBC equity (Rs 77.4 cr) is stated.
